title: The Ultimate Guide to Layering Fragrances
excerpt: Master the art of combining multiple perfumes to create a truly unique, signature scent that is entirely your own.
content:
Layering fragrances is a time-honoured technique used by perfumers and fragrance enthusiasts alike to create complex, multi-dimensional scents. Done right, it allows you to craft a truly personal signature fragrance that no one else wears.

Start with the Foundation

Begin with a base note-dominant fragrance — something woody, musky, or ambery. Think sandalwood, oud, or vetiver. Apply this to your pulse points first and allow it to settle for 2–3 minutes.

Add the Heart

Layer a floral or spicy heart note on top. Rose, jasmine, and cardamom work beautifully over woody bases. The combination creates depth that neither fragrance achieves alone.

Finish with the Top

A light citrus or aquatic spritz on top adds freshness and ensures the opening impression is bright and inviting before it dries down to your layered masterpiece.

Kenyan Climate Tips

In Nairobi's cooler evenings, heavier orientals and ouds project beautifully. On the coast in Mombasa's humidity, lighter citrus and aquatic combinations stay fresh and comfortable all day.

The best perfume is the one that smells like you — Coco Chanel

title: Top 10 Long-Lasting Perfumes for Kenya's Weather
excerpt: Kenya's diverse climate — from Nairobi's cool altitude to Mombasa's coastal heat — demands fragrances with serious longevity. Here are our top picks.
content:
Not all fragrances perform the same in every climate. Kenya presents a unique challenge: Nairobi sits at 1,795m altitude with cool, sometimes chilly evenings, while coastal towns like Mombasa are hot and humid year-round. Here is what works.

For Nairobi

Heavier oriental and woody fragrances shine in Nairobi's temperate climate. The cooler air helps projection without the fragrance becoming overwhelming. Armaf Club De Nuit Intense is a perennial favourite — its smoky, dark berry opening with a sandalwood drydown lasts 12+ hours easily.

For the Coast

On the coast, lighter Eau de Toilettes and fresh aquatics are your friends. Heavy ouds can become cloying in heat and humidity. Opt for citrus-forward fragrances with a clean musk base.

Our Top 5 All-Rounders

These perform well across Kenya's varied climates and are available in our collection: Armaf Club De Nuit Intense Man, Lattafa Asad, YSL Y EDP, Burberry Hero EDP, and Swiss Arabian Oud Wa Atoor.

title: Understanding Eau de Parfum vs Eau de Toilette
excerpt: Confused by fragrance concentrations? We break down the key differences and help you choose the right strength for your lifestyle and budget.
content:
Walk into any perfume counter and you'll be confronted with the same question: EDP or EDT? The difference matters more than you might think — both for how long the fragrance lasts and for how much you spend per wear.

Fragrance Concentrations Explained

Fragrances are classified by the percentage of aromatic compounds (the "juice") suspended in alcohol. Higher concentration generally means stronger projection and longer longevity.

  • Parfum / Extrait — 20–30% aromatic compounds. The purest, longest-lasting form. Apply sparingly.
  • Eau de Parfum (EDP) — 15–20%. The sweet spot for most luxury fragrances. Lasts 6–10 hours.
  • Eau de Toilette (EDT) — 8–15%. Lighter, fresher, more casual. Lasts 3–6 hours.
  • Eau de Cologne (EDC) — 2–4%. Very light, great for hot days. Lasts 1–2 hours.

Which Should You Buy?

For Kenya's climate, we recommend EDP versions for evening wear and special occasions, EDT for daily office use. On a hot Mombasa day, even a light EDT will project well.
author: Scent Mist Kenya
